name: Armyworms
description:
Armyworms are damaging, lawn-feeding pests that emerge in HOT weather. They feed on grass blades in one area until
their food supply is exhausted, often devouring an entire lawn, then move on to the next available lawn.
Discolored grass is often the first sign of armyworms. The damage usually begins along one edge of the turf area. Large
numbers of birds in a turf area may also be a sign of infestation, since armyworms are a source of food for the birds.
Green fecal pellets can often be seen in areas of damage. An infestation can be hard to detect as the caterpillars migrate
to new feeding areas in the cool of the night. Damage can occur rapidly and unexpectedly. Armyworm infestations may
not occur every year in the north.
doWeTreat:
Yes, but coverage will vary by branch. Check TruView shopping cart for availability. If not available in the
cart, set up a property visit request to the branch.

name: Bahiagrass
description:
Bahiagrass is a warm season grass primarily found in Florida and throughout Southeast Georgia. It prefers direct sunlight
and warm temperatures. Not a common grass-type due to sensitivity to weather and products.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans but it needs to be identified prior to service.

name: Bentgrass
description:
Creeping Bentgrass is a soft lime-green turfgrass. It can form an attractive lawn if it is the only variety of grass present,
for example, on a golf course putting green. Usually, Bentgrass is a nuisance in a customer’s lawn because it doesn’t
blend well with other grass types, and it requires so much care. Bentgrass is sensitive to warm temperatures, turns brown
in the summer heat and can be susceptible to diseases such as dollar spot.
doWeTreat:
Yes, this grass type can benefit from our lawn plans, alongside significant maintenance from the homeowner.
TruGreen does not selectively remove Bentgrass from cool season turfgrass lawns.

name: Bermudagrass
description:
Bermudagrass is a warm season grass that is the most common type of grass in the southern US. It is heat and drought
resistant and prefers full sunlight, so will perform poorly in low temperatures and the shade. In the heat it grows quickly,
requiring more frequent mowing than other grass types, yet is wear tolerant. Bermudagrass will go dormant in cooler
temperatures.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Billbugs
description:
Billbugs can damage the lawn in the larvae or grub stage. They will burrow inside the stem and eat the plant from the
inside out, leaving the grass brown, brittle and easy to break off. Lawn damage will appear as spotty patches or yellow or
dead grass, often near sidewalks and driveways, although the entire lawn can be affected. In the North, they prefer
Kentucky Bluegrass and feed from July to August. In the South, they prefer Bermudagrass and Zoysiagrass. Damage can
commonly be mistaken for drought stress.
Do We Treat: Yes, it is included in plans with preventative Grub treatments or as an expanded service.

name: Bindweed/Morning Glory
description:
Bindweed, often referred to as Morning Glory, is a difficult to control perennial weed that grows along a deep, extensive
root system and is composed of vines of arrow-shaped weeds and trumpet shaped flowers. The thread-like vines wrap
themselves tightly around plants or other upward objects.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use pre-emergent and post-emergent weed control to combat this weed and often require multiple
treatments to keep them under control. It can also be treated by removing it, roots, and all, before it germinates. We only
treat for bindweed if it is growing in the lawn.

name: Bluegrass
description:
Bluegrass, also known as Kentucky Bluegrass, is a cool season grass grown in the Northern & Transitional zones. It
prefers full sunshine so has poor shade tolerance. It also prefers cool temperatures. Kentucky Bluegrass requires at least
1-2" of water per week to stay green and should be mowed at 3-4". Warm temperatures and lack of moisture will cause
this grass type to quickly turn brown and enter dormancy.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Buffalo Grass
description:
Buffalo grass is a North American prairie grass suited for semiarid areas of the Great Plains and West. It is a warm season
grass that requires low maintenance once it’s established and is tolerant of alkaline soils but has poor shade tolerance.
Not a common grass for home lawns.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Bugleweed
description:
Bugleweed (Ajuga) is a compact, dense groundcover with beautiful small clusters of purple flowers. It is a fast-spreading,
aggressive ground cover that can quickly take over if not given room to roam.
doWeTreat:
No, TruGreen does not offer a service to keep this ground cover in check and we do not remove weeds from
groundcovers.

name: Centipede Grass
description:
Centipede Grass is a warm season grass that grows primarily in the Southeast due to soil and climate requirements.
Popular along the coastal areas of Carolina, Georgia and the Florida Panhandle, Centipede tolerates heat well but also
needs acidic soil to thrive. Centipedegrass is also characterized by slow growth and poor wear tolerance. During the
winter, it is susceptible to winter injury and severe disease issues in the Spring and Fall.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Chamberbitter
description:
Chamberbitter is also known as Gripeweed, Leafflower or Little Mimosa. It is a warm season, annual, broadleaf weed that
emerges from warm soils beginning in early summer. It tends to germinate in late spring/early summer and can be harder
to remove - needing a combination of manual removal and product to fully eradicate. It is prevalent across the southeast
- from Virginia to Texas.
doWeTreat:
Yes, but due to its nature, customer can ensure eradication by also removing the plant by its roots and using
proper watering/mowing techniques.

name: Chickweed
description:
Chickweed is a cool season, broadleaf weed that prefers moist, well-watered soil and is common in the spring. It has
small succulent leaves, small white flowers, and grows low to the ground in dense patches. Chickweed is common in bare
areas of the lawn. Recommend a fall aeration/overseeding to fill in bare areas.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use pre-emergent and post-emergent weed treatments to combat this weed. It may take multiple
applications to control this weed.

name: Chinch Bugs (Southern)
description:
Chinch Bugs (Southern) are small lawn-damaging insects that feed on the grass blades, causing turf to wilt, turn brown
and die in small, irregular patches. Chinch bug damage is often mistaken for drought damage because chinch bugs are
most damaging during hot and dry weather, and they target stressed areas. The patches will get bigger, even if the lawn
is watered. These pests are mostly found in Florida, Texas and along the coast of the Carolinas and Georgia, where St.
Augustine grass grows.
doWeTreat:
We offer preventative Chinch Bug control as part of the lawn plan or as an expanded service in areas with
St. Augustine turf.

name: Clover
description:
Clover is a weedy ground cover that appears as three leaflets with flowers that are round, and colored white, yellow or
reddish pink. Clover can be common in lawns that are thin, under fertilized or have received excessive moisture.
doWeTreat: Yes, but these weeds can be difficult to treat and require multiple applications to be controlled.

name: Clump Fescue
description:
Tall Fescue is a common turfgrass in the Northern & Transitional regions. It is Clump Fescue when it shows up on a lawn
of Bermudagrass or Kentucky Bluegrass, where it is considered a weed. Tall fescue forms a clump and does not spread
on its own.
doWeTreat:
Not in cool season lawns, it requires a non-selective herbicide that needs to be applied by the customer.
TruGreen can then follow up with a tailored lawn plan to restore the lawn. Tall fescue can be removed from warm season
lawns in the south.

name: Crabgrass
description:
Crabgrass is an annual weed that germinates in the spring/summer and grows wide and flat in the heat of summer if not
controlled. It is lime-green in appearance and typically grown along edges next to hard surfaces. It will take advantage of
any bare or damaged area in the lawn. It thrives in sandy, compacted soil with thin grass and plenty of sunlight.
doWeTreat:
Yes, it is a stubborn weed that requires multiple applications to be controlled. It is best addressed through
the pre-emergent applications applied during the spring, so late season purchasers may struggle more with controlling
this weed.

name: Creeping Charlie
description:
Creeping Charlie, also known as Ground Ivy, thrives in moist and shady areas. It blooms from April-June and can spread
quickly. Its leaves are characterized by round, scalloped edges and are deeply veined. Creeping Charlie can be found
across the US.
doWeTreat:
Yes, however it may require multiple applications to control this weed. Customers can also pull out the plant
by the root, making sure to get all parts of the plant.

name: Cypress Spurge
description:
Cypress Spurge is an invasive broadleaf weed that can be difficult to control. The best way to control the spread of such
weeds is to dig up the plant to remove its extensive root system and prevent continued spread. Also, you can mow down
these weeds while in their flowering state but avoid them when they go to seed as mowing will only encourage the spread
of such weeds.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat Cypress Spurge.

name: Dallisgrass
description:
Dallisgrass is a vigorous grassy weed that grows throughout the southeastern US and parts of the transition zone. It easily
spreads by underground rhizomes. Hand pulling is an option, but if rhizomes are left in the soil, then the weed will regrow.
This weed is very difficult to control with selective herbicides on the market, although TruGreen continues to partner with
universities and suppliers to find breakthrough solutions to control this weed responsibly.
doWeTreat:
Only in specific markets utilizing a specific product on Bermudagrass lawns. A non-selective weed control
option can be used to kill these weeds, but TruGreen does not use these products on lawns as they can damage more
than just the weed.

name: Dandelions
description:
Dandelion is a common perennial broadleaf weed with roots that grow deep into the soil similar to a carrot. It can be found
across the US and in almost all conditions. It prefers sunny areas with good drainage and tends to have very long and
ragged leaves that appear before the flower. The flower will go to seed as temperatures warm. New plants can grow from
seed each year.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use post-emergent weed treatments to combat this weed. It can take multiple applications for these
weeds to be controlled.

name: Deadnettle
description:
Deadnettle is a broadleaf weed also known as Red Deadnettle or Purple Nettle, due to its purplish flowers and reddish or
purplish-tinged leaves. An aggressive, upright weed that prefers moist, shady areas of the lawn. It can usually be found
under trees and shrubs, where grass is sparse.
doWeTreat:
Yes, our post-emergent weed control can address, but this weed is a winter annual, so an ongoing annual
program is recommended.

name: Dollarweed
description:
Dollarweed is a summer perennial weed that thrives in wet areas - often in thin lawns, gardens, and unplanted areas. It
has bright green, round leaves that appear like silver dollars. Due to its love of water, it has a hard time invading properly
irrigated lawns.
doWeTreat:
Yes, but it may take 2 applications, and we recommend aeration to help thicken the turf to ensure Dollarweed
cannot invade in the future. Since Dollarweed loves water, drainage improvements may be required as well.

name: Driveways/Sidewalks
doWeTreat: No, we do not treat driveways/sidewalks. The products that we use are labeled for use in lawns only.

name: European Crane Flies
description:
European Crane Flies can damage a lawn when in their larvae feed on grass roots and cause thinning areas. Healthy,
vigorous turfgrass can withstand low to moderate populations. Damage often becomes noticeable in March and April and
appears as dying patches of turfgrass.
doWeTreat:
Grub preventatives will not control craneflies because the timing of egg laying does not match. If the customer
is already dealing with an infestation, then a property visit is recommended to diagnose the problem and come up with a
treatment plan. Craneflies larvae (leather jackets) can be treated curatively.

name: Fine Fescue
description:
Fine Fescue is a cool-season grass that prefers shade and cooler temperatures but does not tolerate high temperatures.
It tolerates drought well and is often blended with Kentucky Bluegrass for shaded lawns.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Foxtail
description:
The Foxtail plant is a grassy weed with a busy, spiked seed head. A coarse, sprawling weed that quickly multiplies and
takes over large swaths of the landscape. It grows best in both moist and dry soils and all sorts of climate conditions.
doWeTreat: Yes, our pre-emergent and post-emergent weed control can address this weed.

name: Fungus
description:
Signs that a fungus may have caused a disease in the lawn include white, yellow, or brown patches or rings that grow
in diameter. Thin patches of frayed, distorted, or discolored grass blades. Gray, black, red, orange, or purple spots
on blades or stems.
doWeTreat:
Yes, TruGreen treats lawn fungus/diseases however this will require a property visit as the treatment protocol
could be as simple as employing proper mowing and watering practices or more involved as applying a fungicide.

name: Goat Head Weed
description:
Goat Head Weeds are often found in dry states out west and are a difficult to control weed. They are also harmful to pets
and livestock as they can be both poisonous and inflict harm with their burrs.
doWeTreat:
No, non-selective weed controls can be used to kill these weeds, but TruGreen does not use these products
on lawns as they can damage more than just the weed.

name: Goosegrass
description:
Goosegrass is an annual warm season grassy weed that thrives in warm conditions. Each plant can produce thousands
of seeds that germinate in the late spring and mature during the summer months.
doWeTreat:
Yes, but this is a very difficult weed to control and requires a special product for eradication. In warm season
lawns, a preemergent would be a better solution.

name: Gravel Areas
doWeTreat: No, we do not treat gravel areas. The products that we use are labeled for use in lawns only.

name: Grubs
description:
White grubs are small, white, C-shaped larvae of a group of beetles known as scarabs. White Grubs feed on the roots of
plants. The first sign of damage is that the grass wilts easily despite watering. Damage symptoms mimic drought stress.
Continued feeding on grass roots will cause the turf to die in irregular patches. The turf will feel spongy underfoot and
birds may begin to feed in the area. With heavy infestations, the turf can be rolled back like a carpet. Animals, such as
skunks, may tear up the turf while looking for grubs and other insects for food. Japanese Beetle eggs hatch into grubs in
midsummer.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we offer preventative Grub control as part of the lawn plan or as an expanded service. We can also
provide curative services if grubs are actively feeding.

name: Henbit
description:
Henbit is a common aggressive, upright weed that prefers moist, shady areas of the lawn. It can usually be found under
trees and shrubs, where grass is sparse.
doWeTreat:
Yes, our weed control can address, but this weed is a winter annual, so an ongoing annual program is
recommended.

name: Hydroseeding
description:
Hydroseeding/Hydraseeding is a planting process that uses a slurry of grass seed, paper mulch, fertilizer, and water to
cover an area quickly. It is often used as an erosion control technique on construction sites, as an alternative to the
traditional process of broadcasting or sowing dry seed.
doWeTreat: TruGreen does NOT Hydroseed.

name: Japanese Clover/Lespedeza
description:
Japanese Clover is a woody, perennial weed that makes its appearance in late summer. It forms a mat on the ground and
prefers thin, dry, compacted earth. Its leaves resemble a clover with its three leaflets and its pinkish purple to white
flowers.
doWeTreat:
Yes, but it can be difficult to address. It requires pre-emergent weed control and aeration since this weed
prefers compacted soil.

name: Japanese Knotweed
description:
Japanese Knotweed is a difficult to control weed that spreads by underground stems. The best way to control the spread
of such weeds is to dig up the plant to remove its extensive root system and prevent continued spread.
doWeTreat:
No, non-selective weed controls can be used to kill these weeds, but TruGreen does not use these products
on lawns as they can damage more than just the weed.

name: Japanese Stiltgrass
description:
Japanese Stiltgrass is an invasive grassy summer annual weed that is difficult to control. Commonly found in shaded and
moist areas, it spreads rapidly in wooded areas or lawns that are struggling. When dealing with a small population, this
weed can be removed by hand before the plant goes to seed but ensure any equipment that touches the weed is cleaned
and the weed is properly disposed of to avoid further spread.
doWeTreat:
Allowing more sunlight and strengthening the turf will help to stop the spread of this problem weed. A few
products can reduce the population, but typically only a non-selective weed control can be used to kill these weeds.
TruGreen does not use non-selective products on lawns as they can damage more than just the weed.

name: Johnsongrass
description:
Johnsongrass is a difficult to control weed as it spreads through underground rhizomes and seed heads. The best way to
control the spread of such weeds is to dig up the plant to remove its extensive root system and keep the plant from
producing seed that can only further the spread.
doWeTreat:
No, non-selective weed controls can be used to kill these weeds, but TruGreen does not use these products
on lawns as they can damage more than just the weed.

name: Kikuyugrass
description:
Kikuyu grass is a warm season grass that spreads quickly and thrives in warm, temperate climates, around the California
coast. It is mainly used in Southern California due to its drought and heat tolerance, but also can be a serious perennial
weed. Because of its texture, Kikuyugrass is often mistaken for St. Augustine grass.
doWeTreat:
No, non-selective weed controls can be used to kill these weeds, but TruGreen does not use these products
on lawns as they can damage more than just the weed.

name: Lambsquarters
description:
A warm season, annual broadleaf weed found in unmown areas. It grows vertically with a gray mealy coating on young
leaves and small, clustered, green flowers on spikes.
doWeTreat:
Yes, the best treatment for this weed is a well-maintained lawn that is fertilized, mowed, and watered but is
also covered by our weed control treatments.

name: Lawn Plugs
description:
A grass plug is an individual plant that is grown in a tray. The size of the plugs can vary but they are usually about the size
of a large cupcake. Grass plugs can be used to introduce new grass into a lawn or to fill in bare areas.
doWeTreat:
TruGreen only provides lawn plugs in some of our Florida branches. This should be set up as a property
visit. The branches that offer this service are (subject to change): Pensacola, Orlando East/West, Brooksville, Tampa
East/West, Lake Wales, Ft Walton, Ft Myers, Jacksonville East, Leesburg, Sarasota, Ocala, Tallahassee.

name: Mole Crickets
description:
Mole Crickets are 1-2 inches long with strong front legs that burrow into the soil to feed on grass roots, often leaving
unsightly trails, thin turf, and dry root systems. They are most active in the Southeast from April through October and
they prefer warm season turf that is growing in sandy soil.
doWeTreat:
TruGreen offers an expanded service to treat lawns that are most impacted by these insects, which are
primarily in the Carolina and Florida region. Service is called Mole Cricket Recurring Control.

name: Moles (animal)
description:
Moles are small mammals adapted to a subterranean lifestyle. They have cylindrical bodies, velvety fur, very small,
inconspicuous eyes and ears, reduced hindlimbs, and short, powerful forelimbs with large paws adapted for digging.
Moles may be viewed as pests to gardeners, but they provide positive contributions to soil, gardens, and ecosystems, including
soil aeration, feeding on slugs and small creatures that eat plant roots, and providing prey for other wildlife. They eat earthworms
and other small invertebrates in the soil.
doWeTreat: TruGreen does not treat for moles. Our grub preventative will not prevent or reduce moles!

name: Moss
description:
This small, leafy plant is often incorrectly referred to as a "fungus". It can be found in damp or shady conditions with low
pH and compacted soil.
doWeTreat: Only in Washington state.
howToCombat:
Rake up the moss, reseed, and correct the acidity of the soil to prevent further issues. Aim for a full
program with aeration, seeding, and a sulfur/pH balancing treatment. Cut back tree limbs to allow more light to reach the
grass.

name: Mowing/Hedge Trimming
doWeTreat: We "grow it, not mow it." We also do not trim hedges or trees as part of our services.
bestPractices:
We recommend mowing frequently enough so that no more than 1/3 of the leaf blade is removed in a
single mowing - more often during periods of growth and only as needed during periods of drought or dormancy. Keep
in mind that certain grasses, such as Bermuda grass, Zoysia grass and Centipede grass, require close mowing to stay
healthy. Allowing these grasses to grow too high will increase the thatch in your lawn. We also recommend leaving grass
clippings behind to recycle nutrients into your lawn but avoid leaving clumps of wet grass that can suffocate the turf.

name: Mushrooms
description:
Mushrooms appear due to a confluence of factors including shade, moisture, and cloudy & rainy weather conditions. They
are generally found in plant beds or around trees and go away naturally when exposed to sun.
doWeTreat:
While we do not treat for them, trimming back trees and shrubs can expose the mushrooms to sun and keep
them at bay. If mushrooms appear on your lawn alongside standing water, then it is likely a sign of compacted soil, which
could be addressed by core aeration. Digging up old dead tree roots and stumps can help prevent mushrooms that are
feeding on the decaying wood.

name: Necrotic Ring Spot
description:
Necrotic ring spot is a lawn disease that primarily affects sodded Kentucky bluegrass lawns in the late-spring and fall. The
disease causes a circular pattern that looks like a frog-eye that can continue to spread through the lawn. Although it is
not often a devastating disease that kills large areas of turf, moderate to severe outbreaks will disturb the appearance of
the turf. Initial outbreaks of the disease normally occur during cool wet weather in spring or fall months.
doWeTreat:
We will apply a curative fungicide as a LAST resort. Regular fertilization, proper watering, and an annual
aeration to improve soil drainage should all be recommended before a fungicide application.

name: Newly Seeded / Sodded Lawns
description:
TruGreen does not treat newly seeded / sodded lawns as this work is often guaranteed by the landscaper who completed
the work. Any treatment on our end would invalidate the guarantee. Furthermore, TruGreen products, especially our weed
control products, are not labeled for such lawns as they may cause damage. TruGreen recommends waiting 30 days to
apply any weed controls and 1 year to aerate a newly sodded lawn.

name: Nimblewill
description:
Nimblewill is a difficult to control, grassy weed that grows in patches and is most obvious in warm summer months when
the cool season lawns they threaten are stressed.
doWeTreat:
Yes, TruGreen can help reduce a Nimblewill population, but it may take multiple applications. It is also
recommended the customer has aeration/overseeding alongside a comprehensive fall fertilization plan to help crowd out
these weeds and keep them from regrowing next season.

name: Nutsedge
description:
Nutsedge is a rapidly spreading, grass-like weed that appears in the summer in the north but can be persistent year-round
in areas of the south. Nutsedge thrives in warm moist conditions so areas that are compacted and have poor drainage will
be prone to this weed.
doWeTreat:
Yes, it is a stubborn weed that requires multiple applications to be controlled. We can knock the weed back,
but complete control is a challenge.

name: Oxalis/Shamrock/Yellow Wood
description:
Shamrocks/Wood Sorrell (Oxalis) is a weedy ground cover that appears as three heart-shaped leaflets that resemble a
clover. It often produces small, yellow, five petal flowers that close at night. This weed typically appears in the summer.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use pre-emergent and post-emergent weed treatments to combat this weed, but it may take multiple
treatments to be controlled.

name: Perennial Ryegrass
description:
Perennial Ryegrass is a cool-season grass known for its ability to germinate quickly. It thrives in areas where summers
are moderate and winters are cool, as it is not extremely cold tolerant. It mixes well with Kentucky Bluegrass.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Pigweed
description: See Lambsquarters.

name: Plantain Weed
description:
Plantain weeds thrive in unhealthy lawns with compacted soil. They come in two varieties, broad and narrow leaf, and can
be found across the US. They can contaminate mowers/lawn equipment so thorough cleaning after use is necessary to
prevent spreading.
doWeTreat: Yes, aeration is the best plan as well as a lawn program that includes fertilization and weed control.

name: Poa Annua/Annual Bluegrass
description:
Poa Annua is one of the most common grassy weeds in the United States. It looks very similar to Kentucky Bluegrass,
except it is a lighter shade of green. Poa produces numerous seed heads and will brown out in the summer due to poor
heat & drought tolerance.
doWeTreat:
We do not treat for Poa annua in the north or in cool season lawns. In the south, pre-emergent weed
treatments in late summer will stop them from germinating. Post-emergent applications in the spring can be used in warm
season turf markets. Mowing cool season grass at 3-4 inches will make the Poa less noticeable.

name: Poison Ivy
description:
This vine grows across the US and can be found in wooded areas, especially at the tree-break line. It is characterized by
three pointed leaflets. “Leaves of three, let it be!”
Note: Dead poison ivy can still be hazardous. Use caution if removing.
doWeTreat: No, we recommend store-bought products labeled for poison ivy control.

name: Pokeweed
description: Pokeweed is a large annual weed with red stems that produces toxic berries.
doWeTreat: No. It’s best to remove by hand using gloves before the weed produces berries.

name: Pythium Blight
description:
Pythium Blight is a lawn disease that can spread rapidly and cause damage in 24 hours. It thrives in hot, wet conditions
and is attracted to areas that are poorly drained, protected with limited air movement, and have overgrown thatch. Limiting
watering and core aeration are often recommended to address this situation.
doWeTreat:
No. It’s too late to treat pythium blight once the disease is active. Reduce watering to prevent it from
spreading.

name: Quackgrass
description:
Quackgrass is a creeping perennial weed grass that blue green in color. It is commonly found mixed into cool season
lawns. Quackgrass typically is found in vacant fields or along roadsides that are not regularly mowed.
doWeTreat:
No. We cannot safely remove Quackgrass from cool season lawns. Proper mowing and the TruGreen
lawncare program will help the desired lawn grasses outcompete the Quackgrass.

name: Ragweed
description:
Common Ragweed can be found across the US and is the source of most fall allergies including hay fever. It can be found
growing in unkempt lawns, fields, and roadsides. It looks like a fern and has a pungent odor.
doWeTreat: Yes, it is a stubborn weed and may require multiple applications to be controlled.

name: Red Sorrell
description:
Red Sorrell, also known as sheep sorrell, is perennial broadleaf weed that is easily identified by its red flowers and arrow-
shaped leaves. Once it begins to flower, herbicide treatments may be ineffective or require multiple applications.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use pre-emergent and post-emergent weed treatments to combat this weed, but it may take the full
season to control.

name: Red Thread
description:
Red thread is a fungal disease that most commonly occurs in late spring and fall. The affected areas have a pink color
from the tiny red threads of the fungus found on the grass blades as the disease progresses. Moist warm overcast
conditions tend to favor this disease. This disease will only kill the blades leaving brown patches in the lawn. Red thread
will not kill the grass plants.
doWeTreat:
Our lawncare program will help keep the lawn healthy and allow the grass to grow out if the disease occurs.
Watering during dry periods and mowing at the proper height can help reduce the disease. Fungicides are rarely necessary.

name: Sandburs
description: Sandburs grow in southern regions with dry, sandy soils and in patchy lawns.
doWeTreat: Set up a property visit request to the branch.

name: Snow Mold
description:
Snow Mold is a lawn disease that occurs as the snow is melting in late winter and when daytime temperatures are between
35-40 degrees. Signs of both pink and gray snow mold are usually most noticeable in the spring when the snow begins
to melt. As the snow melts, straw-colored circular patches ranging in size from a few inches to several feet across
appear in the lawn. The grass in these patches is usually matted down and crust. Snow mold will only kill the grass blades
and not the grass plants.
doWeTreat:
No. Customers should be encouraged to rake the affected areas to allow the sun to warm the soil and
promote air flow. The grass will recover quickly once the soil temperatures increase. Fertilizer from our TruGreen
lawncare program will promote fast recovery.

name: Sod
description:
Sod is grass and a small part of the soil beneath it held together by the root system and harvested into rolls. It is used to
establish a lawn quickly, especially in areas where seed would be too expensive or not available. Most common types of
sod are St. Augustine, Bermuda, and Centipede.
doWeTreat:
TruGreen does not put down sod. Homeowners should wait until their new sod is fully established to purchase
any of our lawn care services. Their focus should be on proper watering and mowing maintenance. The timeline to start
up with lawn care services will vary, but the homeowner should consider any guarantees offered by their sodding provider.
That said, it’s best to wait a year before signing up for any lawn care services.

name: Sod Webworms
description:
Sod Webworms chew on grass blades when in their caterpillar stage before they turn into moths. Damage first appears
as small, ragged brown spots in the turf, then becomes larger and may join other large dead patches of grass. The
presence of birds or large numbers of moths in the late evening may suggest a Sod Webworm infestation. In the South,
topical sod webworms prefer St. Augustinegrass and can damage throughout the year. In the North, they threaten Fine
Fescue and Bluegrass during the summer months.
doWeTreat:
Yes. Lawn inspection is required. In Florida & Savanah, GA, these insects are covered as part of the
preventative Chinch Bug control application. Chargeable applications will vary across other branches.

name: Soil Sampling
description:
Does TruGreen do soil samples or other soil testing? The short answer is no.
Soil samples/testing:
•
Is not included as part of our standard program
•
Is not advertised as part of TruGreen lawn services
•
Should never be provided as a feature or benefit
•
Is not part of the first service assessment conducted by the specialist
•
Should not be offered as an enticement to start with TruGreen
Sometimes, customers may think that soil testing is needed in their area. A well-maintained lawn does not need ongoing soil testing.
Further, we do not do soil testing even if the customer asks – any customers that request this should be referred to their specialist.

name: Spurge/Spotted Spurge
description:
A spotted weed that thrives in the heat of summer, spotted spurge (Euphorbia maculata) is an unsightly nuisance that not
only takes up residence in weak areas of the lawn, but also invades landscape beds, sidewalk cracks, and vegetable
gardens. Spotted spurge is easily recognized by its hairy red stems that branch out from a central point, tiny dark green
leaves with a red spot, and dense, mat-like shape. This annual weed germinates in mid-spring and produces
inconspicuous, tiny green flowers all summer long. In addition to its signature red spots, spotted spurge can be
distinguished from other weeds by the milky sap that is produced when any part of the plant is damaged. In thin areas of
the lawn, it can form a thick mat that can be up to 3 feet across.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use post-emergent weed treatments to combat this weed. It may take multiple applications to control
this weed.

name: St. Augustine Grass
description:
St. Augustine grass is most popular in the Southern regions due to its tolerance to heat, humidity, and salt. It grows best
in the heat of summer and can produce heavy thatch that requires aeration to break up. It may become dormant and
discolored in the winter.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Tall Fescue
description:
Tall Fescue is a cool-season grass that is durable due to its coarse texture, making for good wear tolerance. It tolerates
drought and heat well - adapting well to either sunny or partially shaded areas. It is not compatible with other turfgrasses
due to its texture and is often considered a weed in finer textured turfgrasses. Tall fescue does not spread so bare spots
will need to be seeded.
doWeTreat: Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.

name: Thistle/Creeping Thistle
description:
Thistle is a thorny broadleaf weed that is also referred to as Creeping Thistle or Canada Thistle. Thistle can release
chemicals into the soil that inhibit the growth of other plants. They tend to take hold on disturbed soils, like field and road
edges, wet and dry sites, pastures, or the yard. It can be found across the US.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use post-emergent weed treatments to combat this weed. It may take multiple applications to control
this weed.

name: Torpedograss
description:
Torpedograss is a perennial grassy weed also known as Bullet Grass, Couch Panicum, Creeping Panic, Dogtooth Grass,
Panic Rampant, and Quack Grass. This grows mostly along the coastal regions of the southern US and prefers marshy
soils.
doWeTreat: Set up a property visit request to the branch.

name: Violets
description:
Wild violets are a perennial broadleaf weed with heart-shaped leaves and a purple flower, which can be white or pink for
some species. It blooms from March through June and can be found in the Eastern half of the US. It prefers shade but
will thrive in full sun areas of the lawn. This weed is very difficult to control and will require multiple applications.
doWeTreat:
Yes - post-emergent weed treatments to control this weed, but it can take a full season to get this weed
under control.

name: Virginia Buttonweed
description:
Virginia Buttonweed is an upright, spreading weed often with yellow-mottled foliage due to a virus. Can have white flowers.
It thrives in wet, moist conditions and tolerates close mowing, so it is found mainly in grass and lawns. This usually grows
along the Southern East Coast and into Texas.
doWeTreat: Yes, it is a stubborn weed and may require multiple applications to be controlled.

name: White Clover
description:
White Clover is a perennial broadleaf weed that grows low to the ground. It has dark green, trifoliate leaves (three leaflets)
with white round flowers with a pinkish cast. It grows in many places, especially sparse lawns where the competition from
grass is weak.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use post-emergent weed treatments to control this weed, but it can take a full season to get this
weed under control.

name: Wild Onions / Onion Grass
description:
Wild Onions / Onion Grass is the most common onion-like winter perennial weed with underground bulbs. They can appear
in lawns but are more often found in flower beds.
doWeTreat:
No, the best method to remove these weeds is to dig up the bulbs; simply pulling from above ground can
cause the bulb to break apart and leave roots behind that can regenerate. You will want to do this before it goes to seed
as that will allow the weed to continue to spread.

name: Wiregrass
description:
Wiregrass, also known as Goosegrass, is a perennial grassy weed. This lawn weed makes its home in sidewalk cracks
and lawns and can be difficult to manage.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we treat this weed when it appears in the lawn, but not on the sidewalks as our products are only
labeled for lawn applications. We highly recommend an annual plan that includes aeration/overseeing to help keep this
weed at bay.

name: Yarrow Weed
description:
Yarrow is an extremely adaptable plant found across the US with a fern-like appearance and a strong sage-like odor. The
tiny seeds are spread by wind and can remain viable in soil for up to nine years. The longevity of the seeds makes complete
yarrow control very difficult.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we use post-emergent weed treatments to combat this weed, but it requires multiple applications to be
controlled.

name: Zoysia
description:
Zoysia is a warm season grass that can tolerate some cooler temperatures - thriving in Southern and Transitional zones.
It prefers sun but can grow in light shade as well and it does not require much water or mowing due to its slow growth.
It can also tolerate drought and high traffic. Zoysia will go dormant and discolor during winter months. Zoysiagrass is not
recommended for the north as its dormancy period will exceed its growing season.
doWeTreat:
Yes, this grass benefits from our lawn plans.
Trees and Shrubs

name: Anti-Desiccant
description:
This treatment will reduce water loss from evergreens and broadleaf evergreen shrubs during the winter months. Extreme water loss during the winter can cause
winter burn. The leaves and needles are coated with a liquid anti-desiccant that prevents water from escaping and thereby reducing the potential for winter burn.
Antidesiccants are applied in November and December before temperatures remain below freezing.
doWeTreat: Not all branches provide this service. Contact the branch for more information.

name: Aphids
description:
Aphids are small, soft-bodied insects that feed by sucking the nutrient-rich liquids out of plants. They multiply quickly and
are found throughout the US.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Apple Scab
description:
Apple Scab is a fungus that attacks the leaves of Crabapple trees. Look for small round brown patches on the leaves. If
untreated, this can lead to complete leaf loss. Fungicide treatments must be made in April – June to be effective.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Arborvitae
description:
Arborvitae is an evergreen coniferous tree which is native to eastern Canada and much of the north-central and
northeastern United States. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental plant.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our standard TruShrub Program.

name: Ash Trees
description:
There are many species of Ash Trees, but the most common are white, black, and green Ash Trees. Their leaves turn
beautiful shades of yellow and burgundy in fall. They are drought tolerant and can be found across the US.
doWeTreat:
Yes, with our standard TruShrub Program. If your TruGreen specialist discovers borer damage, they may
also recommend our Emerald Ash Borer treatment which is NOT included in the standard TruShrub program.

name: Azaleas
description:
Azaleas are spring flowering shrubs that bloom in a variety of colors. Azaleas bloom in the spring, their flowers often last
for several weeks. Shade tolerant and prefer acidic soils.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our standard TruShrub Program.

name: Bagworms
description:
Bagworm caterpillars make distinctive 1.5- to 2-inch-long spindle-shaped bags that can be seen hanging from twigs of a
variety of trees and shrubs. Bagworms prefer Juniper, Arborvitae, Spruce, Pine, and Cedar but also attack deciduous
trees. The bagworms can defoliate plants in a short period of time. These pests are typically active in June and July.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.
whereLocated: East of the Mississippi river.

name: Bamboo
description:
Bamboo is a type of grass with a hard, woody, hollow stem. It is a perennial evergreen, meaning it grows every year and
stays green year-round. Hundreds of kinds grow in different regions of the world, and people have used them in everything
from construction to medicine. Bamboo prefers well-watered, mildly acidic soil in most cases. There are dozens of varieties
of bamboo, with experts asserting that there are over 1,400 different types.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat Bamboo plants.

name: Barberry
description:
Barberry is a thorny deciduous shrub that can range from 1-5' in height. The leaves can be red, green, yellow, or
variegated.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Blight
description:
Blight is a range of tree diseases that can attack leaves and fruit, causing it to discolor and wilt. More serious cases
cause branches to die.
doWeTreat:
No, proper treatment for such diseases will vary based on the type of blight disease affecting the tree so
this will require a property visit to properly diagnose the issue and determine a potential treatment plan.

name: Blue Spruce Trees
description:
Blue Spruce, also known as Colorado Spruce, is a conical-shaped evergreen tree with stiff, horizontal branches and short,
stiff needles. It is commonly used in Midwest landscapes.
doWeTreat:
Yes, with our TruShrub Program; however, certain diseases cannot be controlled such as Cytospora canker.
We will avoid spraying the trees with dormant oil because this application can remove the blue off the needles. Your
TruGreen specialist will also look for signs of Needlecast.

name: Boring Beetles
description:
Wood-boring beetles are species and families of insects, whose larva (in most cases) or adult forms feed off and destroy
wooden materials. The most common types include longhorn beetles, bark beetles and weevils.
doWeTreat: Set up a property visit request to the branch.
whereLocated: Across the US.

name: Bottlebrush Buckeye
description:
The Bottlebrush Buckeye is a species of large suckering deciduous shrub. The species is native to the southeastern United
States, where it is found primarily in Alabama and Georgia, with a disjunct population in South Carolina along the Savannah
River.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat Bottlebrush Buckeye.

name: Boxwood
description:
Boxwood shrubs are slow-growing plants with dark green glossy leaves. Some varieties have variegated leaves. Leaf
shape depends on the variety; some are round while others are elliptical. They provide thick cover because the foliage
begins close to the ground and is dense enough to block light.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.
mainIssues:
Psyllids, Aphids, box tree moths, boxwood
blight

name: Caterpillars
description:
A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth. It’s the second stage in its four-stage life cycle of egg, larva, pupa, and
adult. Caterpillars are insects, just like their parent butterflies or moths. They have six proper legs, like all insects, but also
up to five pairs of stumpy prolegs with little hooks that help them to hang onto things, and to move in a wave-like motion.
Caterpillars eat mostly plants. Many species have a favorite plant, such as a type of tree or grass, or even stinging nettles.
These are known as host plants. The butterfly or moth will lay its eggs on a host plant, so the caterpillars have a ready
source of food when they hatch.
doWeTreat:
Yes, with our TruShrub Program. This is mostly a spring to early summer pest, so round 3 in the north and
rounds 3 & 5 in the south would be the applications that would target these.

name: Cherry trees – non-edible fruit bearing
description:
Cherry Blossom trees bring billowy pink and white blooms in the spring. These blooms often last no more than 2 weeks.
Ornamental cherry trees do not produce edible fruit. TruGreen will not treat edible fruit bearing cherry trees.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Coneflower
description:
Echinacea is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the daisy family. It has ten species, which are commonly called
coneflowers. They are found only in eastern and central North America, where they grow in moist to dry prairies and open
wooded areas.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat Coneflowers.

name: Crabapple Tree
description:
Crabapple are common ornamental trees that are grown in the north. They come in a variety of forms and can grow up
to 20 ft tall. They are widely grown for their attractive growth habit, spring flower display that can range from white to pink
to reg, and decorative red or gold fruits. The most common problem is apple scab disease.
doWeTreat:
Yes, with our TruShrub Program. Some states may consider crabapples to be fruit bearing trees which limits
our ability to treat them.

name: Crape Myrtle
description:
Crape Myrtles are flowering trees that come in a variety of colors and are prevalent in the southern US. They range in size
from dwarf selections that grow less than three feet tall to several varieties that reach upwards of 30 feet. Common
problems are powdery mildew and crape myrtle scale.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Dogwood Trees
description:
Dogwoods are spring flowering ornamental trees that produce a large display of white, pink, or red flowers. The most
common problem is dogwood anthracnose.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Emerald Ash Borer
description:
The Emerald Ash Borer is a green jewel-like beetle native to northeastern Asia that feeds on various species of Ash trees.
The adult beetles nibble on ash foliage but cause little damage. The larvae, however, feed on the inner bark of Ash Trees,
disrupting the tree's ability to transport water and nutrients.
doWeTreat:
Set up a property visit request to the branch. This is a specialized treatment that is not included in the tree
and shrub program. Not all branches are equipped to treat for Emerald Ash Borer.
whereLocated: Eastern and Midwest US.

name: Ground Cover
description:
Ground covers are ornamental, perennial plants that are intended to cover an area of ground for many years. EX: Creeping
Thyme and Ice Plant. They are low (typically less than two feet) spreading plants.
doWeTreat: No. Pachysandra may be treated in some areas due to certain disease and insects.

name: Gypsy Moths (Spongy moths)
description:
Gypsy Moths, also known as spongy moths, as caterpillars, are about two inches long with blue and red dots on their
backs. They feed from late April to mid-June. The caterpillars defoliate (remove leaves from) trees, leaving trees vulnerable
to diseases and other pests, and can eventually kill the tree.
doWeTreat: We will treat trees that are less than 25’ tall. TruGreen does not treat trees that are larger than 25’ tall.
whereLocated: Eastern and Central US.

name: Hibiscus
description:
Hibiscus is a genus of flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae. The genus is quite large, comprising several
hundred species that are native to warm temperate, subtropical, and tropical regions throughout the world. Member
species are renowned for their large, showy flowers and those species are commonly known simply as "hibiscus", or less
widely known as rose mallow. Other names include hardy hibiscus, rose of Sharon, and tropical hibiscus.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Hydrangea
description:
Hydrangeas are popular shrubs with colorful flowers that bloom through summer and into fall. They usually bloom in
shades of blue, purple, and pink, with some selections in white, green, or red. Most hydrangea bushes are easy to grow
and prefer partial shade.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Japanese Beetles
description:
Japanese Beetles are iridescent green beetles that emerge in early July and can be very active for about 6-8 weeks. They
can cause damage to several hundred different types of plants by skeletonizing the leaves (see image to the right). The
grubs develop in the soil, feeding o the roots of various plants and grasses and often destroying turf in lawns.
doWeTreat:
Yes. Damage to trees and shrubs from adult beetles can be minimized with our TruShrub program, which
provides protection.
whereLocated: Across the US, however not as much in Florida.

name: Japanese Maple
description:
The Japanese Maple is considered a small tree, typically growing from 5 to 25 feet (1.5 to 7.5 m.) tall. Their delicate, often
purple leaves turn a shade of red, orange, or yellow in the fall. They are susceptible to wilt and fungus from improper
watering/care.
doWeTreat: No. We do not treat or fertilize Japanese maples.

name: June Bugs
description:
The name "June bug" refers to any of the 100 species of beetles that are related to the scarabs familiar from ancient
Egyptian iconography. Other common names for the June bug include "June beetle" and "May beetle." The common June
bug is one-half to five-eighths inches long and reddish-brown in color. Being beetles, they also sport shiny wing covers,
called elytra. June bugs can cause damage to gardens, lawns, and pastures. They are classified as chafers, meaning they
feed on vegetation, specifically leaves. Their diet can also encompass grass, flowers, fruit, food crops such as grains
(wheat, corn, etc.), sap and decaying organic material. June bugs are nocturnal. They feed from dusk through the evening
hours to avoid predators.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat for June Bugs.

name: Juniper shrubs
description:
Junipers are evergreen shrubs that thrive in most US growing zones. Junipers are versatile and a great for adding depth
and color to any landscape. Junipers are deer resistant, salt tolerant, and extremely low maintenance. Helpful for
controlling soil erosion, Juniper plants are an excellent choice for planting on hills and slopes.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Kudzu plant
description:
Known as “mile-a-minute” and “the vine that ate the South,” this creeping, climbing perennial vine terrorizes native plants
all over the southeastern United States and is making its way into the Midwest, Northeast and even Oregon.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat or control Kudzu plants.

name: Leafminers
description:
The leafminers are a large group of insects that have evolved an interesting approach to survival and reproduction.
Instead of feeding on foliage like many other insects, leafminers live and feed inside the leaves. There are various types
of leafminers, and the adults are either moths, sawflies, flies, or beetles.
Many ornamental trees and shrubs are attacked. Leafminer feeding results in dead tissue in the leaf with a characteristic
feeding track left by each species. A light infestation will not cause much damage but when several generations build up
on a plant, severe leaf browning and leaf drop can occur.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Lilac
description:
The common lilac is well-loved for its toughness, reliability, and fragrance. In fact, lilacs are so tough that they can grow
for 100+ years, often outliving the homes they were planted around. This deciduous multi-stemmed shrub (or small
tree) has about 10 canes and produces flowers at eye-level. The common lilac grows between 8 and 12 feet tall,
depending on the variety. The fragrant flowers are good for cutting and attractive to butterflies. The most common
problem is powdery mildew.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Magnolia trees
description:
Magnolia trees are deciduous and evergreen trees and shrubs that can most accurately be described as magnificent
flowering plants. Magnolia trees are diverse in leaf shape and plant form, and they include both evergreen and deciduous
sorts. Magnolia hardiness varies by species, but most of them thrive in full sun or partial shade with regular water. Main
issues: Magnolia Scale.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Monkey Grass
description:
Monkey grass, also known as Liriope, lilyturf, and blue lily turf, is a grass-like flowering plant that is mainly used as a
ground cover border. Liriope is a tough, adaptable plant that is maintenance free once it is established. The grass-like
leaves stay nice well into the winter months. They are evergreen in warmer climates and semi-evergreen in cooler growing
zones.
doWeTreat: No, we do not treat Monkey Grass.

name: Needlecast
description:
Needlecast is a common fungal disease on Colorado spruce including blue spruce. The disease causes the previous year’s
needles to fall off in the summer. This will be most dramatic at the bottom of the tree. Needlecast attacks trees under
stress in the spring and early summer. Customers must allow at least two years to see the results from our tree and shrub
program.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub Program.

name: Oak Wilt
description:
Oak wilt is an aggressive disease that affects many species of oak (Quercus spp.). It is one of the most serious tree
diseases in the Eastern United States, killing thousands of oaks each year in forests, woodlots, and home landscapes.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat Oak Wilt or any wilt diseases.

name: Palms
description:
Palms are not actually trees. They are considered perennial flowering plants and are mainly found in tropical/subtropical
locations.
doWeTreat: Yes, if under 25 feet tall with our standard TruShrub Program.

name: Pine Bark Beetles
description:
Pine Bark Beetles are insects that normally attack stressed and dying pine trees and usually do not infest trees that are
otherwise healthy and vigorous. They feed and breed in the inner bark of pine trees, and introduce symbiotic fungi into
the tree, often causing or hastening the death of the tree as a result.
doWeTreat: No, TruGreen does not treat for Pine Bark Beetles.

name: Pine Trees
description:
Pine trees are one of the most wide-spread and varied native trees in North America. These cone-bearing evergreens
generally have needle-like leaves, and a single straight trunk, with lateral branches.
doWeTreat: Yes, if under 25 feet tall with our standard TruShrub Program.

name: Rose of Sharon
description: See Hibiscus

name: Roses/Rose Bushes
description:
Rose bushes are woody perennial flowering plants. There are over 300 species. They grow in bushes with thorns on the
flower stems. Rose bushes can range in size from miniature to seven feet tall climbing roses. They are also delicate and
need special care.
•
A shrub rose is typically hardier than other roses. While some will stay in the form of a shrub, others will climb
and grow as tall as 15 feet. Common varieties are Knockout roses and Wiltshire.
•
Bush Rose is a term used to describe modern roses that are smaller than shrub roses. These plants are great
for growing in containers and are an excellent choice for small growing locations. Bush roses can be a smaller
type of shrub rose or even a hybrid tea rose variety. They won’t usually grow taller than 6 feet, which explains
why they’re such a great choice for container gardens or small gardening areas. Popular varieties of bush roses
are the Sunflare and Fairest Cape.
doWeTreat:
Yes, shrub roses such as Knock Out Roses planted in landscapes are included in the tree and shrub program.
Hybrid tea, floribunda and grandiflora roses are not included in the program and will not be treated.

name: Ruby Loropetalum
description:
Ruby Loropetalum is an evergreen shrub found in the South that produces fragrant pink flowers in the spring alongside
green and purple foliage.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub program.

name: Rust fungus
description:
Rust on trees is a fungal infection that causes orange pustules to form on leaves, stems, and branches. Rust can affect
many different types of trees and plants, including crabapples, hawthorns and ornamental pears. Rust rarely kills plants,
but it can cause stems to dieback in severe cases.
doWeTreat:
Yes, we do treat for rust in our TruShrub program. Applications must be made soon after the leaves expand
in the spring.

name: Scale
description:
Scale are tiny sap-sucking insects that can cause damage by draining nutrients from the host plant. Adults form a covering
over their bodies which makes control challenging. Soft scales produce a sticky honeydew that leads to black sooty mold
on leaves. Hard scale does not produce honeydew but can be more challenging to control. Depending on the type of scale
insect, some are easy to control, most require multiple treatments, and there are select ones we may not be able to
control. While customers usually seek out services when there is an issue, the optimal approach is preventative including
dormant oil to limit certain types of scale.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub program.

name: Spanish Moss
description:
Spanish moss is an Epiphyte (a plant that grows on another plant without directly gaining nourishment from it). Spanish
moss receives all of its nutrients and moisture from the air and is not considered a parasite to the tree, it only uses the
tree for support. The only damage it may cause is by breaking a weak limb. Spanish moss is part of the bromeliad family
which places it in the same plant family as pineapples and succulent house plants. Spanish moss is actually native to
Mexico, Central America, South America, the United States and the Caribbean where it can grow in a tropical environment.
doWeTreat: No, we do not control Spanish Moss.

name: Spider Mites
description:
Spider Mites can be a major problem on many woody ornamental plants. Feeding by Spider Mites causes discoloration,
dirty appearance, and early leaf drop. They are related to spiders, are extremely small, and are difficult to detect. They are
typically active starting late Spring and can last through Fall.
doWeTreat: Yes, with our TruShrub program.

name: Spotted Lanternfly
description:
The Spotted Lanternfly is an invasive plant hopper species that has become common in Pennsylvania and several other
nearby states. Adults have black heads and grayish wings with black spots. When flying, they will display red hind wings.
They feed on plants by piercing stems and leaves and leave behind a sticky residue called honeydew, which can attract
bees, wasps, and feed mold. They can often be found swarming in masses over an infested plant.
doWeTreat:
Yes, this is a special treatment available in some areas. Check the shopping cart for availability. If it is not
available, set up a property visit.

name: White Fly
description:
White flies are sap-sucking insects that are often found in clusters on the undersides of leaves. They have wings and can
be as small as 1/12 of an inch. They scatter when disturbed. They damage plants by sucking the juices from new plant
growth, causing stunted growth, leaf yellowing and reduced yields. They secrete honeydew, which can cause leaves to be
sticky or have a black mold.
doWeTreat:
Yes, but only in accordance with our TruShrub Program guidelines (e.g., we will not treat them if on edible
plants or fruit trees).
Pests
whereLocated: In the south, they are found year-round. In the North, they are only found year-round in indoor gardens.

name: Big Head Ants
description:
What are they: Big-headed ants are soil-nesting ants, commonly found nesting outdoors beneath stones, logs and old
timbers. These ants also are commonly found inside the soil of potted plants. In addition, big-headed ants may be found
nesting beneath slab foundations.
whereLocated: Southeastern states, mostly Florida.
howToCombat: Our Flea & Tick Control will combat them.

name: Black Widow Spiders
description:
What are they: Black Widows are poisonous spiders that have a skeleton outside their body, a segmented body, and eight
jointed legs. They are NOT insects. Their deadly poison is said to be 15 times stronger than rattlesnake venom. Black
Widows get their name from the popular belief that the female eats the male after mating, a phenomenon which rarely
happens in nature.
whereLocated:
The Southern black widow is highly concentrated in the Southeastern states but goes as far north as New
York and as far west as Arizona. Northern black widows reside mostly in New England and Southeastern Canada but have
been spotted as far west as Texas and as far south as Florida.
howToCombat:
TruGreen does not directly treat black widows where they live, which tend to be in protected areas such
as crawl spaces or wood piles. Our TruBarrier Perimeter Pest Control only creates a barrier around the house to keep
them from coming in.

name: Box Elder Bugs
description:
What are they: Wood-boring beetles are species and families of insects, whose nymphs (in most cases) or adult forms
feed off and destroy wooden materials. Nymphs (immature) will be red in color and adults will be black with red marking.
It’s common to find these on the warm side of a building in the fall. This insects are not harmful and do not feed on live
plants.
whereLocated: Across most of the Eastern and Mid US.
howToCombat: TruBarrier Perimeter Pest Control

name: Bumble Bees
description:
What are they: A bumblebee is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, one of the bee families. Unlike Honeybees,
Bumblebees are robust, large in girth, have more hairs on their body, and are colored with yellow, orange, and black. They
are typically not aggressive and rarely sting. They also usually nest underground.
whereLocated:
Across the US and most active during warmer months.
Do We Treat: TruGreen takes pollinator protection very seriously. We do NOT treat for pollinators as they encourage plant
growth and are good for the environment. Additionally, we do not treat flowering plants when pollinators are present.

name: Carpenter Ants
description:
What are they: Carpenter Ants get their name from their nest building, where they will excavate the wood and form
smooth tunnels inside the wood. Carpenter Ants do not eat wood, they only tunnel and chew through wood to create
nests.
whereLocated:
Across the US. They appear from May until August in the eastern United States and from February through
June in the west.
howToCombat:
We do not treat for carpenter ants because they are a wood damaging pests. TruBarrier Perimeter Pest
Control will prevent them from entering a home. Also, remove sources of water and wood piles from around the house.

name: Centipedes
description:
What are they: Centipedes are elongated segmented creatures with one pair of legs per body segment. All centipedes
are venomous and can inflict painful bites, injecting their venom through pincer-like appendages known as forcipules.
Despite the name, no centipede has exactly 100 pairs of legs; number of legs ranges from 15 pairs to 191 pairs, always
an odd number. They are predominantly carnivorous.
whereLocated:
Centipedes have a wide geographical range and are found in terrestrial habitats from tropical
rainforests to deserts.
howToCombat: TruBarrier Perimeter Pest Control

name: Chiggers
description:
What are they: Chiggers are the juvenile form of a species of mite that belongs to the Trombiculidae family. They attach
themselves to humans and feed on skin cells, which can lead to itching. They are active from spring until the first frost in
fall.
whereLocated: Across the US – usually near damp, grassy areas and at the edge of forests.
howToCombat:
Our Flea & Tick Control program will prevent chiggers from coming onto the property by treating for
these pests at the source.

name: Chironomid Midges
description:
What are they: Also called "blind mosquitoes", "chizzywinks,", or "fuzzy bills", midges are non-biting insects in the fly
family Chironomidae that breed in natural and constructed bodies of water. Their larvae are also known as "bloodworms".
They are a pest in the south where they can congregate in large masses.
whereLocated: Usually found near water but can be found inland near man-made bodies of water as well.
howToCombat: We do not treat for midges. Our exterior pest control services will not control the source of these insects.

name: Cicadas
description:
What are they: There are over 3400 species of Cicada across the US. They spend most of their lives underground and
emerge in 3–17-year cycles when the ground reaches 64 degrees. They are not lawn damaging, however may damage
ornamentals or large trees (like Maple, Elm, or Oak).
whereLocated: Across the US, but active at different times.
howToCombat: We do not treat for Cicadas.

name: Cicada Killer Wasps
description:
What are they: Cicada Killers are also known as digger wasps and tend to be solitary, living in burrows. These wasps are
large and can be intimidating but are not aggressive like other wasps. They will be typically found in early summer making
burrows in sandy soils.
whereLocated: Across the US.
howToCombat: We do not treat for cicada killers.

name: Clover Mites
description:
What are they: They are a nuisance pest and are a member of the arachnid family; they do not bite or pass diseases to
humans. They do, however, invade in very large numbers and can get into fabrics and furniture, and can cause irritation
in some people.
whereLocated:
Across the US. Abundant in well-fertilized lawns, Clover Mites get into houses through cracks around
windows and doors.
howToCombat: Flea & Tick Control program can prevent Clover Mites from becoming a nuisance.

name: Earwigs
description:
What are they: Commonly referred to as pincher bugs, they are medium-sized insects that have flat bodies (like silverfish)
and are usually black or brown. Earwigs are nocturnal feeders that dine on other insects, as well as vegetation, decaying
organic material — think mulch or piles of leaves — and may also feed on greasy food items.
whereLocated: Across the US.
howToCombat:
Our TruBarrier Perimeter Pest program will help prevent Earwigs from infesting homes with its multi-
layered approach.

name: Fire Ants
description:
What are they: Fire Ants are social and colony forming insects. Adult red imported fire ants are reddish to dark brown
and can vary in size. Eggs are only produced by the queen and hatch into legless larvae that are cared for by the worker
ants. Fire ant stings usually occur when a fire ant mount is disturbed and can be very painful.
whereLocated:
Fire ants can be found in most of the southern United States and in a few areas of New Mexico and
California.
howToCombat: TruGreen uses Top Choice by Bayer to suppress fire ants for a full year.

name: Fleas
description:
What are they: Fleas are small, wingless, and about 2.5 mm long. They feed on blood and can bite pets and humans. Flea
bites may leave the host with numerous swollen, itchy marks. They may cause allergic reactions in some people and can
transmit several diseases.
whereLocated: Across the US.
howToCombat:
Our Flea & Tick Control program will control flea populations by treating for these pests at the source.
However, this service will not control fleas that have become established inside a home..

name: Gnats
description:
What are they: Gnats are small flies in the suborder Nematocera that include midges, crane flies and mosquitoes. They
are often confused with many other types of flying insects. Because of their small size, they are commonly referred to as
‟no-see-ums.” Some of the more common species include fungus gnats, black gnats, drain flies, midges, sand flies and
fruit flies.
whereLocated: Across the US.
howToCombat:
Not directly however, Bifenthrin is a product also used to treat Gnats so TruDefense may help control
Gnats. This would NOT be guaranteed as they are not a targeted pest.

name: Grasshoppers
description:
What are they: Grasshoppers are among what is possibly the most ancient living group of chewing herbivorous insects.
Grasshoppers are typically ground-dwelling insects with powerful hind legs which allow them to escape from threats by
leaping vigorously. Grasshoppers have chewing mouthparts that remove large sections of leaves and flowers, sometimes
devouring entire plants. Garden damage is usually limited to a few weeks in early summer immediately after weeds dry
up.
whereLocated:
In North America, the American grasshopper is found east of the Great Plains, throughout the southeast
and north to near Iowa and Pennsylvania. It is common throughout Florida and is also found in Mexico and the
Bahamas.
howToCombat:
Our Flea & Tick Control and TruBarrier Perimeter Pest Control will control grasshoppers if they are present
at the time of service. It is important to set proper expectations with the customer about where we treat as neither service
treats the lawn. We do not guarantee that our services will prevent grasshoppers.

name: Honeybees
description:
What are they: Honeybees are social insects that live in colonies. The hive population consists of a single queen, a few
hundred drones, and thousands of worker bees. They are slender in body appearance, have fewer body hairs and wings
that are more translucent. They can only sting once and have nests that are above ground. These bees produce edible
honey.
whereLocated: Across the US and most active during warmer months.
howToCombat: We do NOT treat for honeybees or any pollinating insects.

name: Hookworms
description:
What are they: Intestinal parasites, but unlike roundworms and tapeworms they can persist and live in the soil and
environment without an intermediate host.
howToCombat: We do NOT treat for hookworms. Customers should consult a doctor or veterinarian as appropriate.

name: Hornets
description:
What are they: Hornets are the largest of the eusocial wasps and are similar in appearance to their close relatives
yellowjackets. Some species can reach up to 5.5 cm in length. They are distinguished from other vespine wasps by the
relatively large top margin of the head. Worldwide, 22 species of Vespa are recognized.
howToCombat: We do NOT treat hornets. Customers should seek a specialized hornet removal service.

name: Kudzu Bugs
description:
What are they: Kudzu bugs suck nutrients out of plants and can produce a nasty smell when threatened. During the warm
summer months, people do not see the bugs. Once fall temperatures start dropping, kudzu bugs congregate in massive
numbers on sun-exposed surfaces to warm themselves. They will often congregate in homes during the winter months.
whereLocated: Mostly in Southeastern states like Georgia and the Carolinas however, they are spreading.
howToCombat:
Our TruBarrier Perimeter Pest program will help prevent Kudzu bugs from infesting homes with its multi-
layered approach.

name: Love Bugs
description:
What are they: Also referred to as kissing bugs, these insects are flies related to mosquitoes. They will attach their bodies
to their mate and fly in tandem together. They have black bodies and red heads, and they are typically 6-9 millimeters in
length. They swarm once in spring and once in late summer.
whereLocated: Along the Gulf Coast of the US, especially in Florida. They love warm, humid conditions.
howToCombat: No, as these are not normally biting insects and do not cause lawn damage.

name: Millipedes
description:
What are they: Millipedes are a group of arthropods that are characterized by having two pairs of jointed legs on most
body segments; they are known scientifically as the class Diplopoda, the name derived from this feature. Each double-
legged segment is a result of two single segments fused together. Most millipedes have very elongated cylindrical or
flattened bodies with more than 20 segments, while pill millipedes are shorter and can roll into a tight ball. Although the
name "millipede" derives from Latin for "thousand feet", no species was known to have 1,000 or more until the discovery
of Eumillipes persephone, which can have over 1,300 legs. There are approximately 12,000 named species classified into
16 orders and around 140 families, making Diplopoda the largest class of myriapods, an arthropod group which also
includes centipedes and other multi-legged creatures.
whereLocated:
Millipedes are found in every U.S. state, including Alaska and Hawaii, as well as in Puerto Rico and the
U.S. Virgin Islands.
howToCombat: TruBarrier Perimeter Pest Control

name: Mosquitoes
description:
What are they: A mosquito is an insect that bites and feeds on the blood of humans and other animals by tracking their
exhaled Carbon Dioxide. They transmit Zika virus, dengue, malaria, West Nile virus, chikungunya, yellow fever, and more.
whereLocated:
Across the US. Mosquitoes can live in almost any environment, except extreme cold weather. They favor
forests, marshes, tall grasses and weeds, and ground that is wet at least part of the year.
howToCombat:
Our TruDefense treatments are guaranteed to significantly reduce populations and help protect the
outdoor environment.

name: Mud Daubers
description:
What are they: Mud Dauber is a common name for a wasp that builds its nest out of mud. This name covers several
wasps such as organpipe, black-and-yellow and blue Mud Daubers. Finding a nest is the most common sign of an
infestation. If the nest has holes, it may indicate that the nest is inactive, as mud dauber wasps create holes when they
leave the nest.
whereLocated: Across the US and most active during warmer months.
howToCombat:
While we would NOT treat live wasps (see Pollinators), our TruBarrier Perimeter Pest program will remove
old nests from around the first level of the structure.

name: Nematodes
description:
What are they: They are multicellular insects with smooth, unsegmented bodies and are often confused with worms.
Some nematodes feed on the outer surfaces of a plant while others burrow into the tissue. Soil-dwelling nematodes are
the most common culprits, but some species can damage plant roots, stems, foliage, and flowers.
whereLocated: Across the US, more prevalent in the North.
howToCombat: We do not treat for nematodes.

name: No-see-ums
description:
What are they: Gnats are small flies in the suborder Nematocera that includes midges, Crane Flies, and mosquitoes. They
are often confused with many other types of flying insects. Because of their small size, they are commonly referred to as
‟no-see-ums.” Some of the more common species include fungus gnats, black gnats, drain flies, midges, sand flies and
fruit flies.
whereLocated: Across the US.
howToCombat: We do not treat for gnats or no-see-ums.

name: Palmetto Bugs
description:
What are they: A Palmetto Bug is the same thing as a cockroach. The term “palmetto bug” is used most frequently in the
Southeastern United States, particularly in Florida. The American Cockroach is most commonly called a "Palmetto Bug"
due to living in Palmetto trees.
whereLocated: Roaches are located throughout the US, "Palmetto Bugs" are usually found in the Southeastern US.
howToCombat: TruBarrier Perimeter Pest will help treat these invaders.

name: Pill Bugs
description:
What are they: Also known as "Rollie Pollies/Roly Polies", Pill Bugs and Sow Bugs are crustaceans adapted to living on
land. They are active at night, live up to two years, and prefer decomposing vegetation as a food source. Seeing a pill bug
in the home usually means that there is a large population outdoors and without a food source, they do not survive more
than a few days indoors.
whereLocated: Across the US, usually near moist and dark environments.
howToCombat:
While not specifically named, Pill Bugs are controlled by the same methods as Sow Bugs and would be
treated under TruBarrier Perimeter Pest.

name: Roaches
description:
What are they: Roaches are insects of the order Blattodea, which also includes termites. About 30 cockroach species out
of 4,600 are associated with human habitats and about four species are well-known pests. Also known as Water Bugs.
whereLocated: Across the US, mostly in dark and damp environments like basements or wood piles.
howToCombat:
TruBarrier Perimeter Pest will help prevent this pest from entering a home unless there is an existing
infestation.

name: Scorpions
description:
What are they: Scorpions are nuisance pests that are closely related to spiders, mites, and ticks. There are about 1,200
scorpion species in the world and 70 species in the United States.
whereLocated: Arid climates and in the American Southwest. Can be found under rocks and in dark areas.
howToCombat: Yes, with TruBarrier Perimeter Pest!

name: Slugs
description:
What are they: Slugs are soft-bodied animals. Depending on the species, adults can be one to four inches long. Outdoors,
they can cause considerable damage to plants in gardens and flowerbeds.
whereLocated:
Across the US. Moist plant debris, underneath rocks, low weeds, mulch, and fallen logs all provide hiding
places.
howToCombat: We do not treat for slugs.

name: Snails
description:
What are they: Snails are soft-bodied animals and have shells and can withdraw inside them. In harsh conditions, they
can seal the shell and stay alive inside for several years. Outdoors they can cause considerable damage to plants in
gardens and flowerbeds.
whereLocated:
Across the US. Moist plant debris, underneath rocks, low weeds, mulch, and fallen logs all provide hiding
places.
howToCombat: We do not treat for snails.

name: Spiders
description:
What are they: Spiders can be an uncomfortable guest in our homes. Spiders are air-breathing arthropods that have eight
legs, chelicerae with fangs generally able to inject venom, and spinnerets that extrude silk. They are the largest order of
arachnids and rank seventh in total species diversity among all orders of organisms.
howToCombat:
TruGreen offers TruBarrier Perimeter Pest Control, which keeps these helpful arachnids outside where
they can help control populations of other nuisance pests.

name: Springtail
description:
What are they: Also known as "Snow Fleas", they prefer moist conditions and decaying logs. They will flock together near
plant bases in the winter and moist areas in the summer. They are not considered lawn damaging pests as they mostly
eat decaying material.
whereLocated: Across the US.
howToCombat: We do not treat for Springtails.

name: Stag Beetles
description:
What are they: One of the largest of the North American beetles, females of this species can grow up to two inches long
and males up to three inches. Males have elongated, antler-like jaws used to fight rivals and attract mates. They spend
most of their life underground as larvae, only emerging for a few weeks in the summer to find a mate and reproduce.
whereLocated:
